    How the model works

    u is the burned fraction of each grid cell, between 0 and 1.

    ∂u/∂t = max( 0, ∇·(D ∇u) − w·∇u + r u (1 − u) )

    Heat spreading to nearby fuel (diffusion), wind carrying the fire (drift w), and local growth until the fuel is used up. Burned ground stays burned, so u never falls. In still air the front moves at

    c = 2 √(D r)

    Each land cover has a still-air spread rate c. With the live forecast, w changes every hour, and D and r are multiplied by a dryness factor s from air temperature T (°C) and relative humidity RH (%):

    s = exp( 0.0338 (T − 25) − 0.0345 (RH − 40) )

    The logged resources, with nᵢ units each building line at ρᵢ and arriving at time aᵢ, have built this much line by time T:

    B(T) = Σ nᵢ ρᵢ max(0, T − aᵢ)

    The fire is contained at the first T where B(T) ≥ P(T), the fire's perimeter. Before that, the extra crews needed (each building ρ, starting at tₐ) are

    N(T) = ⌈ (P(T) − B(T)) / (ρ (T − tₐ)) ⌉
